claims.claim: Mobileye's Q2 2026 Form 10-Q states that substantially all current revenue is still derived from commercially deployed ADAS/Premium ADAS solutions while Surround ADAS, SuperVision, Chauffeur and Drive are only approaching start of production. This creates a transition-risk test: the future mix depends on successful SOP, OEM ramp and adoption of newer products rather than today's revenue base already proving that mix shift.
causalEdges: current revenue concentration in deployed ADAS -> dependence on legacy/core volumes -> near-term resilience
advanced-product SOP/ramp -> revenue-mix transition -> higher-value autonomy monetization if execution succeeds
claims.falsifier: Reported production ramps and material revenue contribution from Surround ADAS, SuperVision, Chauffeur or Drive would reduce this transition-risk concern.

claims.claim: The same Q2 filing says Mobileye generates the majority of revenue from EyeQ SoCs sold to OEMs through Tier 1 suppliers using volume-based pricing. This is source-addressed concentration in an automotive production channel and exposes results to OEM production volumes, program timing and mix even when design wins remain intact.
causalEdges: OEM/Tier-1 production channel -> vehicle build volumes and program timing -> EyeQ shipment revenue
volume-based pricing and product mix -> realized ASP/margin -> operating economics
claims.falsifier: A more diversified recurring/software/service revenue mix or demonstrated reduced sensitivity to vehicle production and mix would weaken this channel-concentration risk.

claims.claim: Mobileye disclosed that as of April 15, 2026 about 7% of employees had been called to reserve duty in Israel and that operations had not been materially affected to date, while continued regional conflict could affect operations and assets. This is a bounded operational-resilience risk with an explicit mitigating observation: disruption had not been material at the filing date.
causalEdges: regional conflict/reserve duty -> workforce availability and operating continuity risk
observed no material effect through filing -> demonstrated near-term resilience -> lower current severity than a hypothetical disruption
claims.falsifier: Continued filings showing no material operational impact, stable staffing and uninterrupted development/customer delivery would further reduce this risk; disclosed material disruption would increase it.

risks: Advanced-product monetization remains a transition to be demonstrated because substantially all current revenue still comes from commercially deployed ADAS solutions.
Majority revenue exposure to EyeQ shipments through automotive Tier 1/OEM channels leaves results sensitive to vehicle production, program timing, mix and volume-based pricing.
Israel-based workforce exposure creates a factual continuity risk, mitigated by the issuer's statement that operations had not been materially affected as of the filing.
unknowns: The filing does not quantify the future revenue mix or margin contribution by Surround ADAS, SuperVision, Chauffeur and Drive at maturity.
The source does not isolate revenue sensitivity to specific OEM production changes or quantify channel concentration by Tier 1 in the cited passage.
Future regional-conflict operational impact is inherently uncertain and should not be treated as a present blocker absent observed disruption.
changedStrategy: Changed source class from prior issuer announcements and transaction/governance evidence to the current SEC operating-risk disclosure, adding revenue-model transition, automotive-channel dependence and observed workforce-resilience evidence without repeating prior robotaxi/Mentee/dilution claims.
